claims.statement: oxyromon supports two networked DAT providers with asymmetric capability: Redump supports both downloading new DATs and refreshing imported ones, while No-Intro supports update-check only because it publishes a summary (profile.xml) but no direct DAT links; `download-dats` without `-u` for No-Intro prints the warning "Not supported", and the mutually exclusive `-n/--nointro` / `-r/--redump` flags each require the other to be absent. Automatically downloading No-Intro DATs is still an open item in the README TODO list.

Provider families map to content types and entry paths: No-Intro (datomatic.no-intro.org) for cartridge consoles/computers, Redump (redump.org) for optical systems, MAME/FBNeo for arcade; only Redump is fetched by oxyromon, so No-Intro, MAME and FBNeo catalogs must be downloaded by hand and brought in through `import-dats`.

Provider provenance is data, not metadata: `systems.url` is copied verbatim from the DAT `<header><url>` ("www.no-intro.org" / "http://redump.org/"), and `find_systems_by_url` is the only mechanism used to scope a command to one provider — the No-Intro update-check candidate list, the Redump update list, and `generate-playlists`, which limits its picker to Redump because multi-disc games only exist there.

The Redump system catalogue `REDUMP_SYSTEMS_CODES` is a compile-time `phf_map!` of exact Redump system name to datfile URL code (e.g. "Nintendo - GameCube" => "gc"), wrapped in `cfg_if!` so that under `cfg(test)` it collapses to the single entry "Test System" => "ts"; this keeps every download test offline and makes a bulk (`-a`) selection iterate exactly one URL, without any production code path differing.

`find_redump_systems(connection, update)` returns catalogue keys whose name is absent from (update=false) or present in (update=true) the set of systems whose url is REDUMP_SYSTEM_URL, sorted by name; the two modes are complementary halves of the catalogue, which is why the web UI's "Update only" switch simply re-reads the list, and why a Redump system imported under a name the catalogue does not hold is never offered for download.

Per-system fetch `download_redump_dat` GETs `{base}/datfile/{code}/` into memory, opens it as a ZIP extracted into a TempDir under TMP_DIRECTORY, then runs `parse_dat(..., skip_header = true)` and `import_dat(..., None, None, force)`; a ZIP with zero or more-than-one entry is reported as a warning and skipped without touching the database, while a body that is not a ZIP returns Err from `ZipArchive::new`.

The download path's only pacing is one unconditional `sleep(Duration::from_secs(1))` at the end of every system, on success and on warning paths alike; there is no retry, backoff, or HTTP status check, and transport failures panic via `reqwest::get(...).await.expect("Failed to download ZIP")` (and the equivalent expect on the No-Intro profile request) rather than returning Err.

`-s/--save <DIRECTORY>` copies the extracted `.dat` file (not the ZIP) into a directory created on demand under its provider file name; this is the only way to retain a fetched DAT because the extraction TempDir is dropped when `download_redump_dat` returns.

Update detection is `is_update`, a lexicographic `new_version.cmp(old_version)` that skips older and equal versions; `create_or_update_system` aborts the entire DAT import (returns None) unless `is_update(...) || force`, so a same-dated or older DAT never overwrites the catalog unless `-f/--force` is passed — and force is threaded only into the Redump update path, never into new-system downloads.

`update_nointro_dats` GETs `{NOINTRO_BASE_URL}/profile.xml`, deserializes it into `ProfileXml` (each `<datfile>` element aliased to a `SystemXml`), and for each database system with url `www.no-intro.org` reports either the version verdict, "System is no longer available" when the profile has no entry with that exact name, or a parse error — it never downloads a DAT.

The `server`/`mcp` features reuse the same two primitives: `find_redump_systems` backs the GraphQL `downloadableSystems(update:)` query and the MCP `downloadable_systems` tool, while `download_redump_system` — which bails with `Unknown Redump system` for names outside the catalogue, since non-CLI callers may pass anything — backs the GraphQL `download_dats` mutation and MCP tool.

The GraphQL `download_dats` mutation returns immediately and runs the fetches on a spawned tokio task, emitting `download_dats_started` then `download_dats_complete` or `download_dats_error` with the failed system names over SSE; individual system failures are collected rather than aborting the batch, and per-system events are deliberately suppressed because the selection can be the whole catalogue. The MCP equivalent refuses with `read_only_denial` when the server runs read-only.

Game-name semantics come from the external `shiratsu-naming` crate and nowhere else: DAT import, sort-roms selection/weighting, the GraphQL `game_information` resolver and the MCP `parse_game_name` tool all walk the same `NoIntroToken` variants (Title, Region, Languages, Release, Flag, Version), so region/language/flag/version semantics are changed in the crate rather than per call site.

At DAT import time only regions are extracted: `get_regions_from_game_name` tries `NoIntroName::try_parse` and falls back to `TOSECName::try_parse`, normalizing the first Region token with `Region::to_normalized_region_string` into hyphen-joined codes (`(World)` => `US-JP-EU`, `(France, Germany)` => `FR-DE`); arcade systems skip parsing and store an empty region string, and a name that fails both parsers is skipped with a warning rather than imported or fatal.

Sorting consumes the same tokens for selection and ordering: `trim_ignored_games` discards games whose Languages token has no code in LANGUAGES (filtered by LANGUAGE_REGEX `[A-Z][a-z]` / VARIANT_REGEX `[A-Z]{2}`), whose Release status is in DISCARD_RELEASES, or whose comma-split Flag token matches DISCARD_FLAGS — using comment substrings instead for arcade — while `sort_games_by_weight` scores parents, broad/narrow region counts re-parsed with `Region::try_from_tosec_region`, version comparison, and preferred flags, highest weight first.

`compare_versions` compares the first `NoIntroVersion` token numerically as (major, minor) parsed to u64 with unparsable or absent parts treated as 0, and a game carrying a version token always outranks one without: `Game (USA) (Rev 2)` beats `Game (USA)` under PREFER_VERSIONS `new` and loses to it under `old`.

Arcade versus console is decided by DAT shape, not provider: `import_dat` passes `!datfile_xml.machines.is_empty()` as the `arcade` flag, so a DAT whose entries are `<machine>` rather than `<game>` sets `systems.arcade = true`, which suppresses name-based region parsing at import and routes sorting through REGIONS_ALL_ARCADE/REGIONS_ONE_ARCADE bios/parent/clone buckets.

A DAT's `<clrmamepro header="..."/>` detector is resolved first as a file next to the DAT and otherwise from the embedded `data/` asset tree (`#[derive(RustEmbed)] struct Assets`), which is why a No-Intro NES DAT referencing `No-Intro_NES.xml` imports a header even when the detector file was not downloaded; the first clrmamepro element with a header attribute wins among several, `-s/--skip-header` disables it, and the Redump download path always skips header parsing.

The download module's tests are declared behind `#[cfg(test)] mod` in `src/download_dats.rs` and use wiremock so no request leaves the machine: the success test mocks `^/datfile/[a-z0-9-]+/$` with `tests/Test System (20200721).zip` and asserts 1 system / 6 games / 8 ROMs plus the `-s` copy; the failures test asserts empty and two-entry ZIPs leave the database empty and a non-ZIP 404 body returns Err; the No-Intro test mocks `/profile.xml`.

`import-dats -u/--update` restricts itself to systems already in the database, skipping (and asserting zero rows created for) DATs whose system name is unknown, while `-n/--name` and `-e/--extension` are rejected for multi-DAT runs and a custom name must not collide with a known system — the manual counterpart to the Redump download/update split.

On an existing system the `force` flag also decides whether customizations survive: a plain update keeps the stored `custom_name`/`custom_extension` (`custom_name.or(system.custom_name)`), while a forced import applies the customizations exactly as given, so an omitted `-n`/`-e` reverts the system to the DAT header values.

The DAT download and import path launches no external program: the Redump ZIP is read in-process by the `zip` crate, and the README's "External programs" section now lists a single optional tool, `ctrtool`, which is probed and used only by `import-roms` for CIA extraction — the format tools oxyromon once shelled out to (chdman among them) were replaced by the crates under `crates/`.

In `download-dats`, `-u` and `-a` are forwarded to both provider branches, but `-f/--force` and `-s/--save` are consumed only by the Redump branches: on the No-Intro path clap accepts them and nothing reads them.

The MCP `onboard_system` prompt decides its first step from the Redump catalogue: `find_redump_systems(connection, false)` is consulted for an unknown system name, and a match instructs the model to call `download_dats` with the exact catalogue name, while a non-match instructs it to locate No-Intro/MAME Logiqx DATs on disk and call `import_dats`.
